source_text: Ac per hoc constat nihil eum de peccato traducis elocutum, quae quamvis copiosa essent, ad probandum nihil Apostolum de naturali, quod esse non potest et a Manichaeis fingitur, sensisse peccato; ex abundantia tamen etiam distinctionem inculcavit non omnes omnino Adae praevaricatione pollutos, quandoquidem etiam de his, in quibus pro iniquitate regnaret interitus, invenirentur plurimi, qui a praevaricatione Adae docerentur alieni.
pass_a_gloss: And through this it stands that he spoke nothing about the sin of the tradux, which things although they would be copious toward proving that the Apostle meant nothing about a natural sin, which cannot be and is invented by the Manichaeans; nevertheless from abundance he also stamped in a distinction that not all altogether were polluted by Adam's transgression, seeing that even from those in whom destruction would reign for iniquity very many would be found who would be taught alien from Adam's transgression.

lemmas.lexica: LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: It is therefore established that he said nothing about sin transmitted by descent. Although these points were ample to prove that the apostle meant nothing about natural sin, which cannot exist and is invented by the Manichaeans, he nevertheless added the further distinction: absolutely everyone was not stained by Adam’s transgression, since even among those in whom destruction reigned because of wickedness, many could be found who were shown to have had no share in Adam’s transgression (compare Romans 5:14).

choices.why: Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
